guide.reason: The development NFS workflow describes Core-reported repository health and policy warnings. Backup and recovery guidance distinguishes the legacy 64 MiB v1 limit from current v2 paged source support, while recording bounded native complete-history promotion; retained runs are read from Core through authenticated pages rather than heartbeat inventory. A bounded post-promotion NFS payload backup and restore passed later. The NFS guide now instructs operators to use a new repository ID for a moved export or filesystem so old points retain their original destination; the guide now covers all four advertised destinations while the final enabled-build and timed gates remain open. The catalog rebuild guide now explains Core-local pending operations, exact retry and refusal of unresolved remote delete records.

api.reason: Changes Controller, Core-local and peer backup repository registration, typed destination sources, transient credential handoff, health and authority capability/transfer contracts. The new authenticated Core peer repository access POST validates exact member destination, generation and identity, transiently prepares a missing local record, and returns bounded access observations; the existing peer backup-operation GET now returns 404 for a missing exact operation so master reconciliation can settle an orphaned request. Controller/Core report and client API shapes are unchanged by these two peer fixes. The existing policy PUT/Core upsert now requires expected_revision and conflicts on stale updates; SMB3 rotation reuses that operation to switch repository_id; Core registration refuses same-ID source or credential-reference changes for SMB3, S3 and SFTP, and same-ID NFS source or observed filesystem identity changes, so retained points remain bound to their original destination. The NFS refusal tightens existing Core registration behavior without a new route or payload. Existing authenticated NFS peer dispatch, member access and promotion carry the master-observed filesystem identity, which updated members compare before owner-marker claims; matching updated Core versions are required because older peers derived identity from source alone. Moves/rotation use a new repository ID. The Run now repair restores the existing 202 acknowledgement behavior without a schema change. The stale-member admission repair uses the existing Core-local repository contract and adds no operator step. Core-local catalog import/rebuild now returns 202/pending while a bounded Core worker scans; operation GET and exact replay use the existing durable receipt, so local response timing changes without a new route. Controller keeps its existing asynchronous operation contract. Paged backup inventory adds `backup-inventory-pages-v1` negotiation, compact agent reports with run/catalog arrays omitted and reported flags false, bounded Core reverse-channel pages, and client GET page objects with generation, filters and explicit changed-generation/oversized-record errors. Older Core keeps legacy array responses; new Core preserves history but reports `backup-history-api` unsupported to an older Controller until it is upgraded.
